One of these two tasks will be performed next. Option 1: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop.
Option 2: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
--- END OF PROVIDED PORTION ---

Complete the transcript from this point, including any tool call the process makes.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller or simpler version of the original problem. Each recursive call works on this smaller piece, gradually moving toward a situation that is simple enough to solve directly. That simple situation is called the “base case,” and it stops the recursion so it doesn’t go on forever. By combining the results of all these smaller calls, the function builds up the final answer to the original problem.
